Energy.decision: Use Energy to define hierarchy, action color, semantic risk, disabled identity, loading identity, borders, and surface contrast. Primary uses sys.energy.action.primary, secondary uses white background with neutral 900 text/border, and outlined uses white background with neutral 200 outline.
Energy.behavior: Primary is action-primary blue filled. Secondary and outlined both keep a white background; secondary uses neutral 900 border/text, outlined uses neutral 200 border with primary text.
Energy.example: Block card uses danger intent; export movements uses secondary or outlined; start route uses primary.
Energy.test: Verify primary uses action-primary blue while secondary and outlined keep white backgrounds and distinct neutral outlines.
Energy.rejectIf: Primary does not use action-primary, secondary/outlined use filled blue, secondary and outlined backgrounds differ, or outlined border is not neutral 200.

Voice.decision: Use Voice to make labels short, verb-first, readable, and role-consistent across densities.
Voice.behavior: Button labels use Ubuntu body/control typography; long labels wrap safely without breaking the control.
Voice.example: Use “Block card”, “Save driver”, “Start route”, not “OK” or “Continue” when consequence is unclear.
Voice.test: Verify label legibility, wrapping, and font mapping across sizes and responsive contexts.
Voice.rejectIf: Generic copy, missing consequence, Edenred display font used for body/control text, or clipped label.

Frame.decision: Use Frame to control button dimensions, padding, gap, radius, touch target, action rows, and responsive composition.
Frame.behavior: Buttons align to containers, support natural or full width, and keep stable layout in rows, sheets, toolbars, and matrices.
Frame.example: Mobile confirmation stacks full-width actions; fleet toolbar keeps natural grouped actions.
Frame.test: Verify no overlap, no horizontal overflow, stable button dimensions, and minimum touch target.
Frame.rejectIf: Hardcoded layout spacing, cramped action rows, horizontal scroll caused by controls, or unstable dimensions.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only to clarify interaction and stacking, not to decorate the component.
Depth.behavior: Hover and pressed states use restrained elevation/inset feedback; overlays and toolbars can override z-index through a component token.
Depth.example: Toolbar ghost actions stay flat; primary dashboard actions can show hover elevation; pressed state uses inset feedback.
Depth.test: Verify rest, hover, pressed, toolbar, and overlay stacking behavior.
Depth.rejectIf: Arbitrary shadows, z-index literals, or elevation that changes hierarchy without interaction.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum to communicate feedback timing, pressed movement, loading activity, and reduced-motion equivalents.
Momentum.behavior: Transitions are explicit properties; pressed movement is tokenized; loading animation stops under reduced motion while state remains clear.
Momentum.example: Save driver shows loading; Start route uses responsive feedback; reduced motion removes spin and movement.
Momentum.test: Verify hover, pressed, loading, and prefers-reduced-motion behavior.
Momentum.rejectIf: transition: all, hardcoded ms/bezier, motion-only meaning, or no reduced-motion path.

State.decision: Use State to resolve the component before visual styling and assistive semantics.
State.behavior: State precedence is disabled > loading > pressed > focus > hover > default.
State.example: Block card goes loading while service responds; permission-blocked action is disabled with reason nearby.
State.test: Verify every documented state and state precedence across variants and intents.
State.rejectIf: State exists only as visual mock, loading equals disabled, or disabled lacks reason.

Tone.decision: Use Tone to match action language and risk language to the product consequence.
Tone.behavior: Default uses neutral direct action; warning uses caution without panic; danger uses repair/consequence language.
Tone.example: Danger action says “Block card” with consequence copy; warning action says “Reset limits” with risk explanation.
Tone.test: Verify labels and adjacent copy follow tone rules for default, warning, danger, and recovery.
Tone.rejectIf: Jokes, vague labels, blame language, or destructive actions without clear consequence.

Growth.decision: Use Growth as adoption and telemetry metadata, not visible decoration.
Growth.behavior: Button emits/declares analytics event and maturity stage while visual UI remains governed by hierarchy, risk, and state.
Growth.example: button.block-card tracks operational action; button.export-movements tracks dashboard utility usage.
Growth.test: Verify event naming exists for product-changing actions and growth metadata does not alter appearance.
Growth.rejectIf: Growth stage appears as decorative UI, missing analytics for critical action, or event name is generic.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol to render Material Symbols by semantic name with accessible fallback policy.
Symbol.behavior: Leading icons use Material Symbols and inherit semantic color from variant/intent; label remains the accessible name.
Symbol.example: block for Block card, route for Start route, download for Export report.
Symbol.test: Verify icon name renders, icon is aria-hidden, and label remains available.
Symbol.rejectIf: Emoji, text glyph, arbitrary SVG, icon-only Button, or missing accessible label.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography to map icon role, density-owned scale, color, and accessible labeling to the button contract.
Iconography.behavior: Icon scale follows Density; icons inherit the label color so danger/warning contrast cannot diverge from text.
Iconography.example: density.sm uses compact icon rhythm; density.md uses normal control icon rhythm; density.lg dashboard and distance contexts use larger icon scale.
Iconography.test: Verify icon scale per Density context and no icon-only Button usage.
Iconography.rejectIf: Icon size hardcoded, icon replaces text, icon role conflicts with action, or icon color does not match label color.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility to guarantee name, role, state, keyboard, focus, contrast, touch target, forced colors, and reduced motion.
Accessibility.behavior: Native button defaults to type button; focus ring is visible; aria-busy marks loading; disabled blocks activation; forced-colors and reduced-motion have fallbacks.
Accessibility.example: Keyboard user can activate Save driver with Enter/Space and see focus before loading starts.
Accessibility.test: Verify role/name, keyboard activation, focus-visible, forced-colors, reduced motion, touch target, loading, and disabled behavior.
Accessibility.rejectIf: No visible label, no focus state, inaccessible loading, color-only meaning, or pointer-only behavior.
